articles.description: Negotiations on the India-US trade agreement are in their final phase, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said. While an announcement isn't imminent, PM Modi and President Trump may speak soon to assess progress on the 'mutually beneficial' deal.

articles.title: US midterm elections 2026: Trump's approval rating falls to record low as 2026 Midterms near
articles.description: A recent AP-NORC poll shows Donald Trump's approval rating has plummeted to 31%, reflecting increasing public dissatisfaction. With midterm elections on the horizon, voters voiced their worries about the economy and rising prices, emphasizing 17% approval for Trump's management of cost of living. In response, White House spokesperson Davis Ingle defended Trumps record by pointing out his significant policy achievements that could influence the forthcoming elections in November 2026.

articles.title: Tax raid finds Rs 4.34 lakh forex; man wins ITAT case with sister-in-law’s help
articles.description: During the operation, officials discovered Rs 1.12 crore in Indian currency and foreign currency worth Rs 4.34 lakh. The man was subsequently taken in for questioning by the tax authorities. Despite the investigation team's acceptance of the explanation, the AO treated both the Indian cash and foreign currency recovered during the search as unexplained money under Section 69A.

articles.title: Global Markets: Asian shares fall after wild swings in bonds, FX before US jobs data
articles.description: Asian stock markets dipped as investors navigated through the turbulence of bond and currency fluctuations. Elevated oil prices, driven by military strains in the Gulf region, added to the market's unease. Speculations around high US Treasury yields and fiscal instability in Europe, especially concerning French bonds, also weighed heavily. Furthermore, traders keep a close eye on upcoming US job data that may sway Federal Reserve policy.

The Labor Department reported a dip in weekly initial jobless claims, indicating a solid labor market. Oil prices surged, raising inflation concerns as Brent crude settled significantly higher. Technology shares also showed strength, particularly after Accenture's positive revenue forecast.

articles.description: Amazon Great Indian Festival 2026 is set to start on October 8 for all customers. The festival will feature significant discounts of up to 80% on various electronics including smartphones, tablets, and laptops. Customers can enjoy additional bank discounts and cashback offers, enhancing savings during the sale. Major brands such as Samsung, iQOO, and Apple will have notable product deals available.

Small-ticket loans drive India's digital lending boom: Average ticket size rises to ₹18,802, says report
articles.description: Digital NBFCs continue to drive India’s personal loan volumes, with small-ticket borrowing remaining a key feature of the segment. The average ticket size rose 15% to ₹18,802 in Q1 FY26-27, even as digital lenders expanded their reach among younger and smaller-city borrowers.

articles.title: ‘I let my team roast me’: Gen Z founder shares unusual workplace rules, says he pays 2X when employees give up a day off to work
articles.description: At just 25, Pratham Jindal from Chandigarh redefines workplace culture by prioritizing employee satisfaction. He champions doubling pay for those who work on their days off and encourages personal connections among team members. His philosophy values team-building and celebratory office events over mere profits, leading him to sometimes part ways with difficult clients for the team's wellbeing.

articles.title: New liquor shops to keep 500-metre distance from schools, religious sites in West Bengal
articles.description: West Bengal has tightened the norms for opening new retail liquor outlets, increasing the minimum distance from schools, colleges and religious institutions to 500 metres in municipal areas and 1 km in other locations. The earlier limit was 300 metres. The revised rule will apply only to new outlets, leaving existing liquor shops unaffected.

articles.title: Will banks be closed every Saturday? PIB fact-checks fake Gazette
articles.description: The PIB confirmed that a government Gazette declaring Saturdays as public holidays for Public Sector Banks is fake.

articles.title: Stealth frigate INS Trishul takes part in bilateral naval exercise 'Varuna' in France
articles.description: The Indian Navy's stealth frigate INS Trishul has taken part in the flagship bilateral naval exercise 'Varuna' in France. The move aims to strengthen maritime and professional ties between the two countries. INS Trishul is the second ship of the Talwar-class stealth frigates and was commissioned into the Indian Navy in June 2003. The exercise conducted professional, sporting and cultural engagements as well as joint operations with French warships at sea.

articles.title: Scotch whisky gets cheaper in India after trade deal with US; check new prices
articles.description: Under the India-UK agreement, the import tariff on British whisky was reduced to 75% from 150%, effectively cutting the rate by half. The tariff is scheduled to decline further to 40% over the next 10 years. However, the reduction in import duty does not result in a similar reduction in the final retail price.

articles.title: October-born kids: Personality, health, career, relationships and what makes them different
articles.description: October babies are often lively, outgoing individuals who highly value fairness and creativity. With nurturing guidance, they flourish in expressing themselves while embracing their uniqueness. As they mature, many are drawn to careers that involve effective communication and interaction with others. Their emotional well-being hinges on maintaining stability and setting healthy limits, making them likely excel in roles as compassionate parents and supportive colleagues.

articles.title: US economy second quarter growth: GDP grows 2.2 percent as consumer spending and business investment rise
articles.description: The US economy grew 2.2 percent in the second quarter from April to June, the Commerce Department announced recently. Consumer spending and business investment helped propel the growth of the economy. The large increases in imports cut into GDP growth. Spending by consumers was up 3.8 percent, while investment by businesses, less housing, climbed 9 percent. The revised estimate was sharply higher than the 1.5 percent the government had estimated in July.

articles.title: Global Market: Kospi falls as oil prices, Middle East uncertainty weigh
articles.description: South Korean shares slipped despite record September exports, as elevated oil prices and uncertainty over Middle East energy supplies weighed on sentiment. The KOSPI fell 0.21%, while the won weakened and bond yields rose. Exports surged 83.5%, driven by semiconductor shipments and strong AI-related demand, but foreign investors remained net sellers.

articles.title: Trump Announces $54 Billion South Korea Investment In Alaska LNG Project
articles.description: President Trump revealed plans for South Korea to invest approximately $54 billion in a natural gas project in Alaska, supported by Senator Dan Sullivan amidst tight Senate races.

articles.title: Woman accepted Rs 27,000 job offer, found another employee earning Rs 33,000 for same role. She confronted HR and got fired: ‘Why is she getting more?’
articles.description: A social media post by Ankit Pandey sparked debate after he claimed an employee was fired for confronting HR after discovering a colleague earned Rs 33,000 for the same role, compared with her Rs 27,000 salary. Pandey attributed the difference to negotiation and hiring factors, while netizens debated whether employees should accept pay gaps, question unequal compensation or handle salary concerns more strategically.

articles.title: Kotak Mahindra Bank shares in focus after lender appoints Anup Kumar Saha as next CEO. Here’s what Nomura and Jefferies expect
articles.description: Kotak Mahindra Bank shares will be in focus after the lender appointed Anup Kumar Saha as its new MD and CEO for a three-year term starting January 1, 2027. Saha will succeed Ashok Vaswani, who has opted not to seek reappointment. Here's what brokerages Nomura and Jefferies said about the leadership transition, its implications for the bank's strategy and investor sentiment.

articles.description: Despite offering steep discounts and having six months of lead time, some retailers say they have struggled to offload non-compliant products in time.

articles.title: US Trade Representative Greer jokes Piyush Goyal is 'trade minister for life' as G20 trade talks open in Milwaukee
articles.description: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer opened a two-day G20 trade ministers' meeting in Milwaukee addressing key issues. During the event, Greer emphasized the need to rethink global trade governance and identified four pressing priorities. Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal participated actively, promoting India's position on trade agreements alongside his counterparts. The discussions included initiatives concerning steel overcapacity, forced labour, and the Most-Favoured-Nation principle.

articles.title: These 18 stocks could be likely beneficiaries as Centre unveils PM Dhara scheme worth Rs 1.86 lakh crore
articles.description: The government’s Rs 1.86 lakh crore PM DHARA scheme is expected to boost renewable energy, power transmission, capital goods and cable companies. Targeting 135 GW renewable power evacuation, 50 GWh storage and 12–13 HVDC projects through 2027–2036, the programme could create substantial long-term order opportunities for infrastructure and equipment manufacturers.

articles.title: Piyush Goyal calls for clear distinction between food supply ‘weaponisation’ and food-security measures
articles.description: Piyush Goyal addressed the G20 Trade Ministers' meeting, focusing on the distinction in food supply chain strategies. He emphasized the need to differentiate coercive actions from legitimate food security measures. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer discussed the implications of food weaponization and structural excess capacity in global markets. Greer also highlighted concerns about the Most-Favored-Nation principle and forced labor impacting trade fairness.
